label: OmniTIK 5 PoE
description: MikroTik OmniTIK 5 PoE (RBOmniTikUPA-5HnD) — 5x 100M RJ45, Wi-Fi 5 GHz. MIPSBE 1-core AR9344.

poe.note: MikroTik prints current limits and an input-voltage range, never a watt ceiling for these four ports: PoE-out Ether2-Ether5, 1 A per port and 2 A total, at the voltage applied to the unit (11-30 V on the 100M model, 12-57 V on the ac model). Multiplying amperes by a nominal voltage would invent a figure the vendor does not publish.

notes: Inlet is `eth1` at 11 W; `eth2`-`eth5` source passive PoE and cannot be fed. https://mikrotik.com/product/RBOmniTikUPA-5HnDr2 (read 2026-11-28): "Number of DC inputs 1 (PoE-IN)", "PoE in Passive PoE", "PoE in input Voltage 11-30 V", "Max power consumption 59 W", "Max power consumption without attachments 11 W"; "PoE-out ports Ether2-Ether5", "PoE out Passive PoE", "Low voltage PoE-Out current limit 1 A", "Max total out (A) 2 A". https://manual.mikrotik.com/hardware/omnitik-series/ : the output voltage equals the input voltage, 1 A per port and 2 A total. The port is named by the RouterBOARD quick guide - "OmniTik accepts 8-30V Passive PoE from a PoE injector ... The First Ethernet port accepts 8-30V DC powering" (https://www.mikrotik-hrvatska.com/dokumentacija/OmniTik-UPA-5HnD-qg2.pdf). Watts follow the applied input voltage, so the budget is marked unknown rather than multiplied out. Before: five silent sockets, guessed at 12.95 W apiece (64.75 W) on a board that publishes 11 W without attachments.
